note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Severe headache for ~3 days; here for assessment and stronger analgesia options.
- History of present illness:
  - Onset: began approximately 3 days ago while at work; developed gradually.
  - Location: generalized but mainly around the right eye.
  - Character: predominantly dull with intermittent sharper pains.
  - Timing: present most of the time, fluctuating intensity; rates pain 8/10.
  - Progression: worsening since onset; worse on waking the morning after it began.
  - Associated symptoms: transient “shooting lights” at onset, photophobia (bright light hurts), feeling nauseated but no vomiting, difficulty focusing; no neck stiffness (patient initially said “yeah” then “no” — conflict noted), no weakness, no speech difficulty.
  - Triggers/relieving factors: tried ibuprofen over last two days with minimal benefit.
- Past medical history / surgeries:
  - No chronic medical conditions reported.
  - No prior diagnosis of migraine (patient reports prior headaches typically responsive to ibuprofen).
  - Family history: mother and sister have migraines.
- Medications:
  - Ibuprofen — dose/route/frequency not documented (patient later stated “three a day”).
  - No regular medications.
- Social history:
  - Lives with three housemates.
  - Employed in IT; extensive computer/screen use; reduced screen brightness due to symptoms.
  - Wears glasses since childhood.
  - Reports increased work stress with new project.
  - Social smoker and social alcohol use.
- Allergies:
  - No known drug allergies.

Objective:
- No formal physical examination or vital signs documented.
- Neurological status from history: patient reports no focal neurological deficits (no limb weakness, no speech disturbance).
- Ophthalmologic status from history: transient visual phenomena and photophobia reported; no reported permanent vision loss or persistent blurring.
- No fever or rash reported.
- Investigations: none performed or documented.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Headache:
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Migraine.
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Tension-type headache.
     - Ocular strain/visual-related headache.
     - Migraine with visual aura.
   - Investigations planned:
     - Headache diary to identify triggers and frequency.
     - Repeat eye test / optometrist evaluation (recommended).
     - No imaging or laboratory investigations documented at this visit.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Optimize analgesia: review ibuprofen dosing (discussed that ibuprofen can be taken up to two tablets three times daily in the visit).
     - Consider prescribing naproxen as alternative NSAID.
     - Consider adding paracetamol or codeine for acute pain if NSAID inadequate.
     - Advise reduced screen brightness and supportive measures.
     - Return sooner if symptoms worsen or red flags develop (new vision loss, focal weakness, marked deterioration).
   - Relevant referrals:
     - Consider prophylactic headache medication if episodes become frequent (to be discussed at follow-up).

2. Visual symptoms (photophobia, transient shooting lights):
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Photophobia and transient visual phenomena associated with migraine.
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Ocular strain related to prolonged screen use or refractive error.
   - Investigations planned:
     - Repeat eye test / optometrist assessment.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Conservative measures (screen brightness reduction, eye check).
     - Monitor with headache diary; reassess with follow-up.

Follow-up:
- Arrange follow-up with clinician in 1–2 weeks to reassess headache frequency and response to treatment; earlier return advised for worsening symptoms or new neurological signs.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs, focused neurological examination, documented ophthalmologic exam, imaging/laboratory evaluation if indicated, exact medication prescriptions and dosages (except where discussed), confirmation whether any prescription was issued at visit.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Neck pain/stiffness: patient gave both “yeah” and “no” responses to neck pain question (conflict noted).
  - Ibuprofen use: initially described as “a few” tablets over two days; later stated “three a day” (clarified but could be interpreted as inconsistent).
- Transcript quality: generally clear with occasional pauses and overlapping conversational fragments; no sections judged incomprehensible.
